topics.title: Data Collection / Display
topics.subject: mathematics
outcomes: Understand mode, mean and median, as measures of location/central tendency and knows how to find them and when to use them. (k, u, s)
Understand range as a measure of dispersion/spread and how to find it. (k, u, s)
Draw and use frequency tables for ungrouped data. (u, s)
Draw and use frequency tables for grouped data. (u, s)
Estimate measures of location and dispersion for grouped data. (u, s)
Calculate the mean using an assumed mean. (u, s)
Draw a histogram with equal class intervals and use it to estimate the mode. (u, s)
Draw a cumulative frequency curve (ogive) and use it to estimate the median. (u, s, v/a)

body.text: The mean is the sum of all values divided by how many there are; the median is the middle value when the data is ordered; the mode is the most frequently occurring value. The range (highest value minus lowest value) measures how spread out the data is.
For the data set 4, 7, 7, 9, 13: mean = (4+7+7+9+13) ÷ 5 = 40 ÷ 5 = 8; median (already ordered, middle value) = 7; mode (most frequent) = 7; range = 13 - 4 = 9.

When data is grouped into class intervals (e.g. 60-64, 65-69, 70-74 heights), the exact values are lost, so the mean is estimated using the midpoint of each class multiplied by its frequency. A cumulative frequency curve (ogive) plots running totals against the upper class boundary; reading across from half the total frequency and down to the horizontal axis estimates the median.

A histogram with equal class widths shows frequency as bar height; the tallest bar's class contains the mode. Assumed mean speeds up mean calculations for large data sets: pick a value near the middle of the data (the assumed mean, A), work out how far each value deviates from A, average the deviations, and add that average back to A.
